title: Hydrology and Water Resources
description: Hydrology and Water Resources balances hydrologic science with civil engineering design: from water-cycle processes and watershed response through flood risk, drainage, groundwater, and resilient water planning.

topics.title: Hydrologic Cycle, Watersheds, and Water Budgets
topics.description: Establish the movement and storage of water across atmosphere, land surface, soils, streams, aquifers, and engineered systems.

children.title: Hydrologic Cycle Components
children.description: This subtopic gives students the physical map of where water goes and how it moves.

children.title: Precipitation, interception, depression storage, infiltration, runoff, evapotranspiration, recharge, and streamflow
Surface water, soil water, groundwater, atmospheric water, and snow/ice storage
Residence time, flux, storage, and watershed outlet
Blue water, green water, baseflow, and quickflow
Watershed Delineation and Basin Characteristics
children.description: Students learn to define the spatial unit before doing any hydrologic calculation.

children.title: Drainage divide, contributing area, subbasin, pour point, and stream network
Watershed slope, channel length, drainage density, basin shape, and time of concentration
Land cover, soil type, impervious area, and antecedent moisture
DEM, contour map, flow direction, flow accumulation, and stream order
Water Budget Calculations
children.description: The point is to use conservation of mass to organize hydrologic inputs, outputs, and storage change.

children.title: Water budget equation, control volume, storage change, and closure error
Annual, seasonal, event, and long-term average budgets
Reservoir, lake, urban watershed, agricultural basin, and aquifer budget
Data uncertainty, ungauged terms, and residual interpretation

topics.title: Precipitation Measurement, Storm Analysis, and Design Rainfall
topics.description: Analyze rainfall data, storm structure, precipitation frequency, and design storms.

children.title: Precipitation Measurement
children.description: Students learn how rainfall and snowfall data are measured and why data quality matters.

children.title: Rain gauge, tipping bucket, weighing gauge, snow pillow, radar rainfall, and satellite precipitation
Point rainfall, areal rainfall, Thiessen polygon, isohyetal method, and radar bias correction
Missing data, double-mass curve, gauge undercatch, and quality control
Storm depth, duration, intensity, and accumulation
Storm Hyetographs and Design Storms
children.description: This subtopic turns precipitation records into engineering inputs.

children.title: Hyetograph, cumulative rainfall curve, rainfall excess, and storm temporal pattern
Intensity-duration-frequency curve, design storm, return period, and annual exceedance probability
NOAA Atlas precipitation frequency estimates
Alternating block method, SCS Type II distribution, and local storm pattern
Extreme Precipitation and Climate Context
children.description: The goal is to interpret precipitation extremes with both historical statistics and changing conditions.

children.title: Stationarity, nonstationarity, trend, climate normal, and climate projection
Probable maximum precipitation as an optional advanced concept
Atmospheric river, convective storm, tropical cyclone rainfall, and snowmelt-rain event
Uncertainty bounds and conservative design choices

topics.title: Evaporation, Transpiration, and Soil-Water Processes
topics.description: Estimate water losses through evaporation, plant transpiration, and soil-moisture storage.

children.title: Evaporation Physics
children.description: Students learn what controls water loss from open water, wet soil, and surfaces.

children.title: Vapor pressure, saturation vapor pressure, relative humidity, and vapor pressure deficit
Net radiation, wind speed, air temperature, and surface resistance
Energy balance, aerodynamic method, pan evaporation, and pan coefficient
Lake evaporation, reservoir evaporation, and evaporation suppression context
Transpiration and Evapotranspiration
children.description: This subtopic connects plant water use to watershed and irrigation calculations.

children.title: Transpiration, evapotranspiration, potential ET, reference ET, and actual ET
Penman-Monteith equation, crop coefficient, and growing season demand
Root zone, stomatal resistance, soil moisture limitation, and vegetation type
Irrigation demand, drought stress, and water supply planning
Soil-Water Storage
children.description: The point is to understand the near-surface reservoir that controls runoff, recharge, and plant use.

children.title: Porosity, volumetric water content, field capacity, wilting point, and available water
Soil texture, soil structure, capillary pressure, and matric potential
Antecedent moisture condition and soil-water deficit
Soil-water balance and root-zone accounting

topics.title: Infiltration, Soil Moisture, and Unsaturated Flow
topics.description: Model how rainfall enters soil and becomes storage, interflow, recharge, or runoff.

children.title: Infiltration Concepts and Measurements
children.description: Students learn how rainfall enters soil and when it becomes runoff.

children.title: Infiltration capacity, infiltration rate, cumulative infiltration, and rainfall excess
Horton infiltration model, Green-Ampt model, and Philip infiltration idea
Infiltrometer, rainfall simulator, and field infiltration test
Crusting, compaction, macropores, and preferential flow
Unsaturated Flow and Soil Hydraulics
children.description: This subtopic introduces the physics of flow through partially saturated soils.

children.title: Unsaturated hydraulic conductivity, soil-water characteristic curve, and capillary head
Richards equation as an advanced reference point
Percolation, interflow, recharge, and perched water
Hysteresis, wetting front, and drainage path
Abstractions in Engineering Models
children.description: The goal is to convert complex soil processes into practical model inputs.

children.title: Initial abstraction, continuing loss, depression storage, interception loss, and infiltration loss
SCS/NRCS curve number, hydrologic soil group, and antecedent runoff condition
Impervious area, directly connected impervious area, and effective imperviousness
Calibration of loss parameters and sensitivity to soil assumptions

topics.title: Runoff Generation, Streamflow, and Hydrograph Analysis
topics.description: Explain how watersheds transform rainfall into streamflow, baseflow, and flood peaks.

children.title: Runoff Generation Mechanisms
children.description: Students learn why different landscapes produce runoff in different ways.

children.title: Infiltration-excess runoff, saturation-excess runoff, subsurface stormflow, and return flow
Hortonian runoff, variable source area, and contributing area expansion
Urban runoff, rural runoff, snowmelt runoff, and frozen ground effects
Land use, soil, slope, and drainage network controls
Streamflow Data and Hydrograph Components
children.description: This subtopic teaches students to read and interpret discharge records.

children.title: Stage, discharge, rating curve, gage height, and streamflow record
Rising limb, peak discharge, recession limb, baseflow, and direct runoff
Baseflow separation, event runoff volume, lag time, and time to peak
Flow duration curve and seasonal streamflow regime
Hydrologic Response Metrics
children.description: The point is to quantify watershed behavior from observed or modeled hydrographs.

children.title: Runoff coefficient, runoff ratio, peak flow, and runoff depth
Time of concentration, basin lag, travel time, and storage effects
Unit peak discharge and hydrograph shape
Flashiness, attenuation, and watershed memory

topics.title: Unit Hydrographs, Rainfall-Runoff Modeling, and Watershed Response
topics.description: Use unit hydrograph and rainfall-runoff methods to predict watershed discharge.

children.title: Unit Hydrograph Theory
children.description: Students learn a classic linear method for converting rainfall excess into runoff hydrographs.

children.title: Unit hydrograph, effective rainfall, direct runoff hydrograph, and duration
Linearity, superposition, proportionality, and time invariance assumptions
S-curve hydrograph and changing duration
Deriving unit hydrographs from observed storms
Synthetic and Empirical Methods
children.description: This subtopic covers practical design methods for ungauged or data-limited watersheds.

children.title: SCS/NRCS dimensionless unit hydrograph, Snyder unit hydrograph, and Clark unit hydrograph
Rational method, runoff coefficient, rainfall intensity, and drainage area
Curve number method, initial abstraction, and rainfall excess depth
Regional regression equations and ungauged basin estimation
Model Calibration and Validation
children.description: The goal is to evaluate whether a rainfall-runoff model is trustworthy.

children.title: Calibration, validation, verification, and parameter sensitivity
Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency, percent bias, peak error, and volume error
Event model versus continuous simulation
Overfitting, equifinality, and uncertainty in model parameters

topics.title: Flood Routing, Streamflow Routing, and Reservoir Operations
topics.description: Route flows through channels, reservoirs, and storage systems.

children.title: Hydrologic Routing
children.description: Students learn how storage changes the timing and magnitude of flood waves.

children.title: Continuity equation, storage equation, inflow hydrograph, and outflow hydrograph
Level-pool reservoir routing, storage-indication method, and spillway rating
Muskingum routing, K and X parameters, and channel storage
Peak attenuation, lag, and travel time
Hydraulic Routing Concepts
children.description: This subtopic gives context for more detailed unsteady-flow models.

children.title: Kinematic wave, diffusion wave, dynamic wave, and Saint-Venant equations
Backwater effects, flood wave celerity, and channel roughness
HEC-RAS context, boundary conditions, and cross-section data
When hydrologic routing is insufficient
Reservoir and Flood-Control Operations
children.description: The point is to connect routing to management decisions.

children.title: Rule curve, flood pool, conservation pool, dead storage, and surcharge storage
Outlet works, spillway, gate operation, and emergency release
Detention basin, retention basin, and dry/wet pond
Trade-offs among flood control, water supply, hydropower, and environmental flows

topics.title: Groundwater Hydrology, Aquifers, and Well Hydraulics
topics.description: Analyze groundwater storage, flow, recharge, pumping, and aquifer response.

children.title: Aquifer Properties and Darcy Flow
children.description: Students learn the main properties that govern subsurface flow.

children.title: Aquifer, aquitard, confined aquifer, unconfined aquifer, and perched aquifer
Hydraulic head, hydraulic gradient, Darcy's law, and specific discharge
Hydraulic conductivity, transmissivity, storativity, and specific yield
Porosity, effective porosity, anisotropy, and heterogeneity
Groundwater Flow Systems
children.description: This subtopic links groundwater to recharge, discharge, streams, and regional flow.

children.title: Recharge area, discharge area, water table, potentiometric surface, and groundwater divide
Flow net, equipotential line, flow line, and seepage face
Baseflow, gaining stream, losing stream, and stream-aquifer interaction
Groundwater age, residence time, and regional flow path
Well Hydraulics and Pumping Tests
children.description: The goal is to estimate aquifer behavior from wells and pumping data.

children.title: Drawdown, cone of depression, radius of influence, and well efficiency
Theis solution, Cooper-Jacob approximation, and specific capacity
Pumping test, observation well, recovery test, and step-drawdown test
Well interference, sustainable yield, and capture zone

topics.title: Water Quality, Sediment, and Watershed Health
topics.description: Connect hydrologic processes to pollutants, sediment transport, temperature, nutrients, and ecosystem condition.

children.title: Water Quality Indicators
children.description: Students learn the basic measurements that describe water condition and suitability.

children.title: Temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, conductivity, turbidity, and total suspended solids
Nutrients, nitrogen, phosphorus, biochemical oxygen demand, and pathogens
Metals, organic contaminants, salinity, and emerging contaminants
Grab sample, composite sample, sensor data, and detection limit
Pollutant Sources and Transport
children.description: This subtopic connects land use and hydrology to water-quality outcomes.

children.title: Point source, nonpoint source, stormwater runoff, and combined sewer overflow
Advection, dispersion, dilution, settling, sorption, and decay
Sediment yield, erosion, bank erosion, and bedload/suspended load
TMDL, load duration curve, and pollutant load estimation
Watershed Health and Ecological Flow
children.description: The point is to see water resources as ecological and human systems together.

children.title: Riparian zone, wetland, habitat connectivity, and stream temperature
Environmental flow, low-flow statistic, and flow regime alteration
Best management practice, buffer strip, detention, and nutrient management
Urbanization, impervious cover, channel incision, and stream restoration

topics.title: Open-Channel Flow, Stormwater, and Drainage Design
topics.description: Apply hydraulic principles to channels, culverts, storm sewers, detention, and urban drainage.

children.title: Open-Channel Flow Basics
children.description: Students learn the hydraulic tools needed for natural channels and drainage infrastructure.

children.title: Open-channel flow, free surface, wetted perimeter, hydraulic radius, and specific energy
Manning equation, roughness coefficient, normal depth, and critical depth
Subcritical flow, supercritical flow, Froude number, and hydraulic jump
Channel lining, erosion protection, and conveyance capacity
Stormwater Drainage Systems
children.description: This subtopic covers engineered drainage in urban and transportation settings.

children.title: Storm sewer, inlet, catch basin, culvert, gutter flow, and spread
Minor system, major system, design storm, and drainage area
Culvert inlet control, outlet control, headwater, and tailwater
Detention, retention, infiltration basin, and outlet structure
Urban Hydrology and Low-Impact Development
children.description: The goal is to manage runoff volume, peak flow, and water quality in built environments.

children.title: Imperviousness, connected impervious area, time of concentration, and flashy hydrograph
Green infrastructure, bioretention, rain garden, bioswale, permeable pavement, and green roof
Runoff reduction, peak shaving, water-quality volume, and first flush
SWMM model concepts and stormwater performance metrics

topics.title: Hydrologic Frequency Analysis, Flood Risk, and Drought Analysis
topics.description: Quantify extremes, return periods, uncertainty, flood risk, and drought severity.

children.title: Frequency Analysis and Design Events
children.description: Students learn to estimate rare events from limited records while acknowledging uncertainty.

children.title: Annual maximum series, partial duration series, return period, and exceedance probability
Empirical plotting position, frequency factor, and design quantile
Log-Pearson Type III, Gumbel, generalized extreme value, and lognormal models
Confidence interval, record length, outlier, and skew coefficient
Flood Risk and Floodplain Management
children.description: This subtopic connects hydrologic estimates to maps, policy, and infrastructure decisions.

children.title: Flood hazard, exposure, vulnerability, consequence, and risk
Base flood, 1-percent annual chance flood, floodplain, floodway, and freeboard
FEMA flood maps, flood insurance rate map, and risk communication
Levee, detention, channel improvement, buyout, and nature-based mitigation
Drought Analysis and Low-Flow Hydrology
children.description: The point is to treat water scarcity as a hydrologic design and management problem.

children.title: Meteorological drought, agricultural drought, hydrologic drought, and socioeconomic drought
Standardized precipitation index, Palmer drought index, and streamflow drought index
Low-flow frequency, 7Q10, flow duration curve, and water supply reliability
Demand management, drought contingency plan, and reservoir storage trigger

topics.title: Hydrologic Data, GIS, Remote Sensing, and Modeling Tools
topics.description: Use observed data, spatial analysis, and models to analyze watersheds and water systems.

children.title: Hydrologic Data Sources
children.description: Students learn where reliable hydrologic data come from and what each dataset can support.

children.title: USGS streamgage, groundwater well, precipitation station, water-quality station, and metadata
NOAA precipitation, radar rainfall, snow data, and drought monitor products
EPA water quality data and watershed datasets
Data cleaning, gap filling, datum, time step, and unit consistency
GIS and Remote Sensing for Watersheds
children.description: This subtopic covers spatial tools used in modern hydrology.

children.title: DEM, land cover, soil map, watershed boundary, and stream network
Flow direction, flow accumulation, slope, aspect, and drainage area
Remote sensing precipitation, evapotranspiration, snow cover, and soil moisture
Spatial resolution, temporal resolution, projection, and uncertainty
Modeling Tools and Workflows
children.description: The goal is to use models transparently, not as black boxes.

children.title: HEC-HMS basin model, meteorologic model, control specifications, and loss/transform methods
SWMM subcatchment, conduit, junction, storage unit, and outfall
HEC-RAS context for hydraulic modeling and floodplain analysis
Scenario setup, calibration, sensitivity analysis, documentation, and reproducible workflow

topics.title: Water Resources Planning, Allocation, and Management
topics.description: Evaluate water supply, demand, reservoirs, legal/institutional constraints, and competing uses.

children.title: Water Supply and Demand Planning
children.description: Students learn to estimate whether water systems can meet competing demands.

children.title: Municipal demand, agricultural demand, industrial demand, ecological demand, and peak demand
Supply source, reservoir storage, groundwater yield, reuse, and interbasin transfer
Demand forecast, conservation, leakage, and per-capita use
Safe yield, firm yield, and reliability of supply
Allocation, Law, and Institutions
children.description: This subtopic introduces the governance layer that shapes engineering options.

children.title: Riparian rights, prior appropriation, water right, permit, and allocation rule
Interstate compact, basin authority, irrigation district, and utility governance
Environmental regulations, drinking water, wastewater, and water quality standards
Stakeholder, equity, tribal water rights, and public participation
Multiobjective Planning and Trade-Offs
children.description: The point is to evaluate water projects as systems with competing objectives.

children.title: Objective, constraint, alternative, performance metric, and trade-off curve
Cost-benefit analysis, life-cycle cost, benefit-cost ratio, and uncertainty
Flood control, water supply, hydropower, recreation, navigation, and ecosystem services
Robust decision-making and adaptive management

topics.title: Climate-Informed Design, Green Infrastructure, and Resilience
topics.description: Design hydrologic systems for changing climate, urbanization, flood/drought stress, and resilience.

children.title: Climate-Informed Hydrologic Design
children.description: Students learn how changing climate challenges stationary design assumptions.

children.title: Stationarity, nonstationarity, trend analysis, and climate-adjusted design storm
Downscaling, climate model ensemble, scenario, and uncertainty range
Sea-level rise, compound flooding, snowpack shift, and extreme precipitation
Adaptive design, safety factor, and design-life risk
Green Infrastructure and Nature-Based Solutions
children.description: This subtopic connects hydrologic performance to ecological and urban design.

children.title: Bioretention, constructed wetland, green roof, permeable pavement, urban tree canopy, and floodplain reconnection
Infiltration, evapotranspiration, detention, retention, and pollutant removal
Co-benefits: heat reduction, habitat, recreation, and water quality
Maintenance, clogging, soil media, and performance monitoring
Resilience and Adaptation Planning
children.description: The goal is to design water systems that can absorb, recover, and adapt.

children.title: Resilience, robustness, redundancy, flexibility, and adaptive capacity
Critical infrastructure, cascading failure, emergency operation, and recovery time
Flood warning, drought trigger, managed retreat, and phased adaptation
Equity, vulnerability mapping, community risk, and resilience metrics
